_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-03-06 17:58:07Z)**_

Here's the command with maximum verbosity and debug output:

```zsh
specstory watch cursorcli \
  --telemetry-endpoint "localhost:4317" \
  --debug \
  --log \
  --debug-raw \
  --console
```

Or using environment variables for the OTEL endpoint:

```zsh
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="localhost:4317" \
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="specstory-cli" \
specstory watch cursorcli \
  --debug \
  --log \
  --debug-raw \
  --console
```

**What each flag does:**
- `cursorcli` — targets Cursor chat history (SQLite at `~/.cursor/chats/`)
- `--telemetry-endpoint` / `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` — your OTLP gRPC collector
- `--debug` — enables debug-level log output
- `--log` — writes logs to `.specstory/debug/debug.log`
- `--console` — streams logs to stdout so you see everything live
- `--debug-raw` — dumps raw SQLite records as pretty-printed JSON to `.specstory/debug/<session-id>/` so you can inspect exactly what the provider is reading and what's being parsed before it hits the OTEL spans

The `--debug-raw` output will be your best tool for diagnosing why tool use isn't making it into the traces — you'll be able to compare the raw Cursor data against what actually gets emitted.

Run this from the root of your test project directory.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-03-06 18:03:15Z)**_

The `cursorcli` provider reads from `~/.cursor/chats/` — that's actually the Cursor IDE's chat history (the SQLite database), not the Cursor CLI. The name is a bit confusing, but `cursorcli` is the right provider for Cursor IDE chat histories.

So the command I gave you is correct — just use `cursorcli`:

```zsh
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="localhost:4317" \
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="specstory-cli" \
specstory watch cursorcli \
  --debug \
  --log \
  --debug-raw \
  --console
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-03-06 19:14:24Z)**_

That warning is harmless for your purposes — it just means your collector at port 4320 supports OTLP **traces** but not OTLP **metrics**. Traces should still be flowing through fine.

This is a separate issue from the tool use not appearing in traces. The metrics warning won't be the cause of that problem.

Are you seeing traces show up at all, just without tool use data? Or are traces not appearing either?
